issue.title: [bug] Web search: raw-utterance query + no result synthesis (context-blind at both ends)
issue.symptom:
Observed in a dashboard chat session (2026-07-01): user gave a multi-sentence
explanation of SAE/Anthropic and ended the turn with a meta-instruction to the
model ("...it would probably be best to do a web search to learn more"). The
web_search tool call fired with the ENTIRE raw turn as the literal query,
including the user's own "you should search" meta-commentary and an unfixed
transcription typo ("Spare Auto Encoder" instead of "Sparse Auto Encoder").

Transcript:
  User: "So, it's called a Spare Auto Encoder. Anthropic designed it to allow
  more fine detailed reading and influence of model inference in process. It
  would be probably best to do a web search to learn more."
  [Searched the web for: So, it's called a Spare Auto Encoder. Anthropic
  designed it ]
  "Here's what I found for so, it's called a spare auto encoder. anthropic
  designed it to allow more fine detailed reading and influence of model
  inference in process. it would probably be best to do a web search to
  learn more:"

No query distillation happened before the tool call — the raw utterance
(including the speaker's own self-referential instruction) was passed through
as search content instead of extracted intent/topic.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via code investigation):
  - gaia-core/gaia_core/cognition/tool_selector.py:217-292
    `_deterministic_tool_match` — a regex/keyword shortcut that bypasses the
    LLM tool-selector "to prevent hallucinated tool calls when the selection
    model is weak" (comment at line 417-418). Triggers on the substring "web
    search" anywhere in the message (line 218). Tries prefix patterns like
    "web search for ", "search the web for " (lines 230-254) to isolate the
    subject; none match when the trigger phrase is buried in ordinary prose,
    so it falls through to line 258: `query = lowered` — the ENTIRE lowercased
    raw message.
  - gaia-core/gaia_core/cognition/agent_core.py:2748-2821 has a near-identical,
    independently-written shortcut with the same failure mode — line
    2761/2769: `_query = user_input  # Fallback to full input`.
  - Display strings that expose the raw query to the user:
    agent_core.py:2818 (`"*[Searched the web for: ...]*"`) and
    agent_core.py:9316-9319 (`"Here's what I found for **{query}**:"`).

FIX: force explicit query-distillation (short topic string, not verbatim
conversation text) before the search fires. Either widen/replace the
prefix-stripping heuristics in tool_selector.py:230-292 and
agent_core.py:2759-2769, or drop the "fallback to raw user_input" behavior
and require the LLM-driven query-extraction path instead.

SECOND HALF OF THE SAME FAILURE — result narration also skips synthesis:
  - agent_core.py:9254 `_deterministic_tool_narration()` — docstring (lines
    9259-9261) explicitly says web_search "DOES benefit from LLM synthesis"
    and should fall through to normal LLM narration. But the actual code at
    line ~9305-9308 special-cases `tool_name == "web" and action == "search"`
    into a raw numbered-list dump of titles/snippets/links (lines 9317-9330),
    with a comment explaining this was a later patch to stop Core E4B from
    degenerating into URL-hallucination loops when asked to freely summarize
    search-result lists. The docstring was never reconciled with this
    special case — right now NO path reaches synthesis for search results,
    contradicting the function's own stated contract.
  - This means results are always shown to the user verbatim (raw
    title/snippet/link bullets) instead of a generated response that
    considers the results in context of what was actually asked.
  - There IS a working precedent for bounded/grounded synthesis already in
    the codebase: the deterministic pre-execution path at
    agent_core.py:2795-2807 fetches the actual top-result page content and
    injects it as a `tool_result` data_field with the instruction "Use this
    content to fulfill the user's request directly," then lets normal LLM
    generation continue — grounded in fetched text rather than free-form
    link-listing, which is presumably why it doesn't degenerate.
  - FIX: reuse that grounded-injection pattern for the
    `_deterministic_tool_narration` web.search branch instead of the raw
    list dump — inject fetched/snippet content + a strict "answer using only
    this" instruction, then let the model generate prose, rather than either
    (a) raw dump (current, context-blind) or (b) fully free-form synthesis
    over a list of links (previously caused the hallucination loop this was
    patched to avoid).

Distinct from a separate same-session non-sequitur (identity question -> "let
me check my memory" -> quantum physics) which is a stale few-shot exemplar in
prompt_builder.py:117-141 leaking into REFLEX-mode responses via proximity
bias — a prompt/system-card issue, unrelated to this ticket, not filed here.

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-core/gaia_core/cognition/tests/test_tool_selector_web_search.py
"""Regression tests for GAIA_Project-h34: the deterministic web-search
query extractor fell back to the ENTIRE raw user utterance (including the
speaker's own "you should search" meta-commentary) whenever the trigger
phrase was embedded in ordinary prose instead of an explicit "search for X"
pattern. Pins the sentence-dropping fallback that replaced it.
"""

from gaia_core.cognition.tool_selector import _deterministic_tool_match


def _query_for(user_input: str) -> str:
    result = _deterministic_tool_match(user_input.lower(), user_input)
    assert result is not None
    assert result.tool_name == "web"
    assert result.params["action"] == "search"
    return result.params["query"]


def test_trigger_sentence_dropped_from_conversational_prose():
    # The exact GAIA_Project-h34 repro: a multi-sentence explanation ending
    # with a meta-instruction to search. The query must not be the whole
    # utterance, and must not contain the speaker's own instruction to search.
    text = (
        "So, it's called a Spare Auto Encoder. Anthropic designed it to "
        "allow more fine detailed reading and influence of model inference "
        "in process. It would be probably best to do a web search to learn "
        "more."
    )
    query = _query_for(text)
    assert "web search" not in query
    assert "it would be probably best" not in query
    assert "spare auto encoder" in query


def test_explicit_search_for_pattern_still_works():
    query = _query_for("Please search the web for Jabberwocky poem")
    assert "jabberwocky" in query
    assert "search" not in query


def test_subject_before_tool_phrase_still_works():
    query = _query_for(
        "Recite Jabberwocky for me? If you're unsure, feel free to use the web search."
    )
    assert "jabberwocky" in query


def test_bare_search_request_falls_back_to_full_text():
    # Nothing but the trigger phrase itself — there's genuinely no other
    # subject matter, so the full (short) text is the only reasonable query.
    query = _query_for("please do a web search")
    assert query

-                if not _query or len(_query) < 3:

+                    _new_query = _re_search.sub(f"(?i){_re_search.escape(_strip)}", "", _query).strip()
+                    if _new_query != _query:
+                        _stripped_any = True
+                    _query = _new_query
+                if not _stripped_any or not _query or len(_query) < 3:
+                    # None of the known strip-phrases isolated a subject —
